cards.body:
## Summary
The UAT's headline number - each journey's pass/conditional/fail - is chosen free-hand by the codex judge. Half of the 84 judged journeys on disk cannot be reproduced from the checks the same run recorded. Make the judge answer atomic named checks (the journey's Definition-of-done bullets, D1..Dn, beside the Character's criteria it already answers) and decide the verdict in code from those checks, the metric gates the DoD states, blocker criteria, breaches and how the journey ended.

## Description
The skill's consistency harness is 'judgement externalized into explicit, scored criteria'. The driver honours that for criteria and metrics, then lets the judge pick the verdict anyway (linga-text.cjs:59). On the committed runs: 15 journeys are 'fail' with every applicable criterion passing, 20 are 'conditional' with every criterion passing, and a rule over the recorded checks (criteria, metric gates, breaches, ending) agrees with the judge on 42 of 84. The missing inputs are the DoD bullets, which the judge reads as prose (linga-text.cjs:441) and never answers item by item. The verdict then feeds three consumers: the report scorecard (linga-text.cjs:206), the per-Character report (:457) and recertify's regression detector (recertify.cjs:212-217), which today flags a regression when a model's mood changes.

The move: a pure uat/driver/verdict.cjs with doneChecks(journeyFile) (the '## Definition of done' bullets become D1..Dn, derived, never hand-copied), gates from a `gates` field in each journey's sim block (J1 placement exact|near, J2 topic fit >= 4/6 and safe = all, J3 pitch >= 0.8 and moments >= 0.9, J5 0 breaches), and verdictOf(record, ctx) -> {verdict, why[], judgeVerdict, agrees}. The judge schema gains done[] with one row per D id (minItems = maxItems, checked in code like prior[]). Code order: not-reached (no judge, setup or model failure) -> fail (ended before done, breach, BLOCKER criterion, failed D check, missed gate) -> conditional (failed ordinary criterion, unanswered D check) -> pass. The judge's own verdict is kept as judgeVerdict, and the report counts where no check explains it: that is a finding about the judge, not about Linga. Decisions stay in code (repo law) - applied to the harness that judges the product.

## Flow
- child: judge answers criteria[], done[] (new), metrics, findings, as before
- verdictOf() decides the verdict and names its reasons; record.verdict + record.verdictWhy saved
- report.md scorecard: 'fail - D2 (#6), pitch 1/4 < 80%' instead of a bare 'fail'; plus 'judge verdicts no recorded check explains: N'
- recertify: Regressed compares code verdicts; a changed judge mood alone is not a regression
- run.json driver hash changes, so recertify.cjs confounds() already marks the instrument change

## Expected impact
Every verdict an operator reads can be traced to a check with step evidence. The 24 committed verdicts that are harsher than every recorded check become either explained (a D row) or visible as judge noise. Recertify stops reporting regressions that no check supports. A driver artefact like the 900-character cut is found from the scorecard instead of by re-reading transcripts.

## Evaluation
Claim: the journey verdict is reproducible from named checks; recertify regressions rest on checks
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass; 42 of 84 committed verdicts reproducible from the recorded checks, 0 of 84 carry a reason
After: 8 of 8; every non-pass verdict carries >= 1 named reason
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.rollback: ledger.cjs and its test are new; recertify.cjs gains planLedger/finishLedger beside the untouched per-run plan/finish, and the driver's no-argument --recertify and --status are new branches. git revert of the series leaves the per-run recertify exactly as it is; committed runs are only read by the tests (temp copies), and a live recertify's stamps are the same fields recertify_run / recertify_status / recertify_evidence it writes today.
cards.runner_up: Every run, not only --recertify, shows each judge its pair's open ledger rows in prior[], so no open row ages unasked and a full run doubles as a recertification
cards.body:
## Summary
An operator who asks 'what is open for Linga, and what do I rerun?' today reads five findings.json files (186 open rows), two hand-written notes (VERIFY.md, recertify.md) and then recertifies one run, which asks about 7 of the 36 pairs that hold open rows. Derive one ledger from every run, give each finding a global id, and turn it into two commands: --status (what is open now, by pair, with how long it has gone unasked) and --recertify with no run (rerun every pair with an open row, each judge answering all of that pair's open rows across runs, stamps written back into each originating run).

## Description
The driver names findings by position (linga-text.cjs:216), so 51 of the 114 distinct open ids name a different finding in each run, and recurrence can only be linked inside one --recertify <run> (recertify.cjs:35-44, 170-182). The five committed runs therefore hold 186 open rows, all recurrence 1, although the operator recorded by hand that two gaps recur across all three runs (runs/2026-09-15-lt/recertify.md:37-39). 30 of the 36 open pairs have open rows in more than one run; tomas-9 J4 has 13 from three runs, and recertifying the newest run asks about 4. Older rows have no door back in. The drain, whose first ranking key is recurrence, has never been run (README.md:67-71 homes absent).

uat/driver/ledger.cjs folds the runs in order (run.json started, else directory name; recert-<k> after its parent) into rows keyed '<runId>/<id>', resolving each recertify stamp and each rerun row's recurs link into one gap chain, and counting for each open row how many later runs ran its pair without asking about it (unasked). planLedger() gives the pairs and their open global ids; finishLedger() reuses priorStatuses() and writes each answer back into the findings.json of the run that owns the row; statusOf() renders the operator view. linga-text.cjs gains `--status` (no model call) and `--recertify` with no run, which places the rerun under the newest originating run as recert-<k> so the existing layout holds.

## Flow
- node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --status -> OPEN.md: 186 open in 36 pairs across 5 runs; per pair, rows by rank with 'unasked since <run>'; drained 0 of 5; the next command
- node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --recertify -> every pair with an open row; each judge sees that pair's open rows from every run (global ids)
- answers stamped into each originating findings.json; recurs chains fold; status re-rendered
- --recertify <run> unchanged for a targeted rerun

## Expected impact
Five reads and a guess become one command, and the rerun covers every open row instead of the newest run's share (36 pairs instead of 7). Recurrence becomes data, so the drain's 'recurrence first' ranking can run from the JSON. Stale rows stop being invisible: each says how many reruns have passed it by.

## Evaluation
Claim: one derived ledger answers 'what is open now' and drives a recertify of all of it
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass; 186 open rows across 5 files, 7 of 36 pairs reachable by one --recertify, recurrence 1 on 360 of 360 rows
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none
